newsitem.title: USA: Perkin-Elmer has higher quarter, year.
newsitem.headline: Perkin-Elmer has higher quarter, year.

text.p: Perkin-Elmer Corp. on Thursday reported higher fiscal fourth-quarter and annual earnings while taking a $24 million restructuring charge to improve manufacturing.

The Norwalk, Conn.-based developer and manufacturer of life science systems and analytical instruments said fourth-quarter net income, excluding special items, increased to $38 million, or 85 cents a share, from $27.6 million, or 63 cents a share, the prior year.
Revenues for the quarter rose more than 13 percent to $347 million from $305 million in last year's fourth quarter.
Perkin-Elmer's fourth-quarter earnings edged the consensus analyst forecast of 84 cents a share, according to market research firm First Call.

"Having substantially increased the profitability and cash flow of the Analytical Instruments Division, we have now begun to examine its product portfolio to determine an appropriate growth strategy for that business," said company Chairman Tony White.

The company's restructuring programme, which resulted in the $24 million charge in the fourth quarter, is proceeding as planned, White said. However, the company remains concerned about the Analytical Instruments division's future revenue growth.
Geographically, the company reported revenue growth in each of its major regions in the fourth quarter. Revenues grew 11 percent in both the United States and Europe, and 27 percent in the Far East.

Without the effect of currency, revenues in Europe and the Far East would have increased 19 percent and 36 percent, respectively. Regions outside the United States accounted for 61 percent of consolidated fourth-quarter revenues, which is consistent with the prior year.
For the full year, including special items in both years, Perkin-Elmer earned $115.2 million, or $2.38 a share, compared with $13.9 million, or 32 cents, a year earlier.
Revenues increased nearly 10 percent to $1.28 billion, from $1.16 billion in fiscal 1996.
Perkin-Elmer stock was down 37.5 cents at $82.25 in consolidated midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
